issues.legal_issue: The acquisition cost of property bought in one currency and sold in another may be converted using a reasonable, reliable conversion schedule to determine taxable profit or loss.
material_facts: The properties were bought during an occupation period using Japanese currency and later sold using Malayan currency.
The tax officer used the conversion schedule accompanying the local debtor-creditor ordinance to convert the acquisition costs into Malayan currency.
The schedule was the only material available to the officer for determining a common currency standard and resulted from an inquiry by responsible authorities.
The taxpayer proposed no alternative conversion basis.
issues.conclusion: The tax officer was justified in using the schedule to ascertain the properties’ acquisition costs in Malayan currency, although the ordinance and schedule were made for a different purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Where property is purchased in one currency and sold in another, profit or loss cannot be determined without converting both amounts to a common standard. A reasonable conversion rate may be drawn from the only available reliable material, including a schedule prepared after a careful inquiry even if it was designed for another purpose. The Court approved the principle applied in S. L. N. Sathappa Chettiar v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Madras, (1959) 35 I.T.R. 641. The Debtor and Creditor (Occupation Period) Ordinance, 1948, and its schedule were relevant as evidence of conversion rates, not as provisions directly governing the calculation.

predicates.income_tax_profit_assessment: A tax assessment requires the profit or loss from a property transaction to be determined.
predicates.property_bought_and_sold_in_different_cu: The property was acquired using one currency and disposed of using another.
predicates.no_parity_between_currencies: The currencies did not have an established parity that would itself provide a common standard for comparing the acquisition and sale amounts.
predicates.schedule_is_only_reliable_conversion_bas: A conversion schedule based on a responsible inquiry was the only reliable conversion material available to the assessing officer.

issues.definition: When an income-tax profit assessment concerns property bought and sold in different currencies with no parity between them, and the only reliable conversion basis is an official schedule, that schedule may be used.

issues.legal_issue: A method used in earlier assessment years does not prevent the tax authority from using the correct method in a later assessment year.
material_facts: The taxpayer said that it had maintained regular accounts and used the original acquisition costs in its business balance sheets in earlier years.
The taxpayer said that the tax department had not allowed a loss based on scaling down the properties’ values in earlier years.
For the assessment year under appeal, the tax officer used the conversion schedule to determine the acquisition costs in Malayan currency.
The Court held that the use of another method in previous years did not prevent the officer from ascertaining and using the correct method for the year under assessment.
issues.conclusion: The tax officer was not prevented from using the correct method for the assessment year merely because a different method had been used in earlier years.
issues.legal_principle: The correct method may be applied to the assessment year in question notwithstanding a different method used in previous years. The Court relied on its conclusion that a common currency standard was necessary to determine the real profit or loss and approved the reasoning in S. L. N. Sathappa Chettiar v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Madras, (1959) 35 I.T.R. 641. The dispute arose through the reference procedure under sections 66(1) and 66(2) of the Income-tax Act, but those provisions did not supply the substantive conversion rule.

predicates.income_tax_profit_assessment: A tax assessment requires the profit or loss for the relevant assessment year to be determined.
predicates.prior_year_method_differed: A method different from the one used for the relevant assessment year was used in earlier years.
predicates.current_year_method_is_correct: The method used for the relevant assessment year correctly determines profit or loss on the facts of the transaction.

issues.definition: In an income-tax profit assessment, a different method used in earlier years does not bar use of the correct method for the current year.
